2026-07-27.title: The Humanoid 100: Mapping the Humanoid Robot Value Chain
2026-07-27.summary: Morgan Stanley's global research team maps 100 public companies across the humanoid-robot value chain — Brain (22 semis/software names), Body (64 industrial-component suppliers: actuators, bearings, screws, reducers, motors, sensors, batteries), and Integrators building full humanoids. Its US TAM model projects 8 million humanoid units by 2040 (~$357B wage impact) rising to 63 million by 2050 (~$3T wage impact, ~$1T annual US humanoid revenue), against a global labor market it sizes near $30T.
2026-07-27.analysis: Metis angle: two of our clients are on the list itself. Regal Rexnord appears in four Body categories (bearings, gears/reducers, motors, complete actuators) and is called a leading US supplier of electric motors, gearing, and linear actuators; Rockwell Automation is listed under Diversified Automation for its sensors-to-software stack. The report's sharpest finding is geographic: 73% of companies confirmed to be involved are Asia-based (56% China), and Morgan Stanley explicitly compares the West's position to its EV supply-chain experience. For engagements with Rockwell and Regal Rexnord, humanoids are both a long-dated demand tailwind for their component portfolios and a near-term strategy question: component orders and partnership decisions arrive years before the 2040-2050 adoption inflection the model projects.

sections.heading: What the report covers
sections.body: The Humanoid 100 is Morgan Stanley's cross-sector mapping of the public companies most exposed to humanoid robots, built with dozens of its sector teams after investor interest surged following Jensen Huang's CES 2025 physical-AI keynote. Companies are grouped into Brain (22 semis and software names), Body (64 industrial-component suppliers), and Integrators (22 companies developing full humanoids). 52% are already reported to be involved in humanoids; the other 48% are close competitors or names MS analysts believe have material potential to enter.

sections.heading: The anatomy: where the value sits
sections.body: The brain combines foundational GenAI models (NVIDIA Gr00t, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft), simulation and digital-twin software for training (Dassault, Siemens, Hexagon), and vision/compute/memory semis. The body is actuators and their parts — bearings, screws, gears/reducers, motors, encoders — plus rare-earth magnets, sensors, wiring, and a lithium-ion battery. Tesla's Optimus Gen2 alone uses 50 degrees of freedom driven by 28 actuators; humanoid makers design proprietary actuators but source components from the same global supplier web as autos.

sections.heading: The geographic imbalance
sections.body: 73% of companies confirmed to be involved (and 77% of integrators) are Asia-based, 56% out of China. Only 31% of the US & Canada names are reported involved, versus 83% of the China & Taiwan names. MS explicitly compares the West's position to its EV supply-chain experience, and notes Chinese startups benefit from established supply chains, local adoption, and state support. The scarcity of Western pure plays beyond Tesla and NVIDIA is itself the finding.

sections.heading: The market model
sections.body: MS assumes a $150k average selling price in 2028 falling to ~$50k by 2040 on an 8-year replacement cycle. Its US TAM model reaches 8 million installed humanoids by 2040 (~$357B wage impact) and 63 million by 2050 (~$3T wage impact), with US market revenue of ~$4B in 2030, ~$240B in 2040, and ~$1T by 2050 — the inflection lands in the 2040s. A parallel China model projects 1.5M/7.4M/59M units by 2030/2035/2050 on faster price declines and lower labor-cost adoptability.

sections.heading: The Metis client read
sections.body: Regal Rexnord appears in four Body categories (bearings, gears/reducers, motors, complete actuators) and is described as a leading US supplier of electric motors, gearing, and linear actuators. Rockwell Automation is listed under Diversified Automation for its sensors-to-software industrial stack. For both accounts this is a long-dated demand tailwind with near-term strategy consequences: component sourcing, capacity, and partnership decisions get made years before the model's adoption inflection — and the report frames exactly which parts of their portfolios the market will price on this theme.
